name: Pediatric low-grade glioma: carboplatin/vinCRIStine backbone, or BRAF-targeted dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E-altered tumors; per-drug doses VERIFY
histology: pediatric low-grade glioma; pilocytic astrocytoma (WHO grade 1) is the most common, arising in cerebellum, optic pathway, or brainstem, and frequently carries BRAF fusions or mutations

biomarkers.BRAF_V600E: tested; if mutated, targetable with a BRAF inhibitor plus MEK inhibitor (dabrafenib + trametinib)
biomarkers.BRAF_fusion: tested; KIAA1549::BRAF fusion is the characteristic pilocytic astrocytoma alteration (MAPK-pathway activating)
biomarkers.NTRK_fusion: tested; NTRK1/2/3 fusion is targetable (TRK inhibitor) where present
biomarkers.note: Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric CNS Cancers v1.2026 and Harrison 22nd ed. Pilocytic astrocytomas frequently harbor BRAF fusions or mutations (harrison.txt lines 102931 and 102937 to 102938: BRAF V600E targetable with BRAF inhibitors). BRAF V600E-mutated pediatric glioma is targetable with dabrafenib/trametinib (ped_cns.txt lines 1203, 1209 to 1211); BRAF V600E and BRAF fusion are listed molecular alterations of significance in pediatric gliomas (ped_cns.txt lines 906 to 907). BRAF is the actionable gate; the carboplatin/vinCRIStine cytotoxic backbone is not biomarker-restricted.

treatmentSetting: primary/adjuvant systemic therapy for progressive, unresectable, or symptomatic low-grade glioma (observation or resection for resectable disease); chemotherapy is preferred over radiotherapy in young children to avoid radiation late effects
lineOfTherapy: first-line for progressive/unresectable low-grade glioma; BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy is an option for BRAF-altered tumors

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: well-demarcated pilocytic lesions may be cured by complete resection; observation with serial MRI for asymptomatic residual disease; systemic therapy for progressive, unresectable, or symptomatic disease
eligibilityCriteria.locator: harrison.txt lines 102926 to 102938 (pilocytic astrocytoma WHO grade 1, potentially curable if completely resected; BRAF fusions/mutations; BRAF V600E targetable) and 103006 to 103008 (observe smaller lesions, resect larger symptomatic lesions)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: in young children, initial chemotherapy is preferred over radiotherapy; vinCRIStine plus carboplatin is the most common first-line regimen for progressive childhood low-grade glioma
eligibilityCriteria.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer 12th ed.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: devita.txt line 241008 (children who receive initial chemotherapy compared with radiotherapy; vincristine plus carboplatin remains the most common first-line regimen) and line 244896 (HIT-LGG carboplatin-vincristine in progressive low-grade gliomas of childhood)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: BRAF V600E-mutated tumors are eligible for dabrafenib + trametinib targeted therapy
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric CNS Cancers v1.2026
eligibilityCriteria.locator: ped_cns.txt lines 1203, 1209 to 1211 (If BRAF V600E mutated: Dabrafenib/Trametinib)

drugs.name: CARBOplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer 12th ed.
provenance.locator: devita.txt line 241008 (vincristine plus carboplatin most common first-line regimen for progressive childhood low-grade glioma); line 244896 (HIT-LGG carboplatin-vincristine); no per-drug dose printed

drugs.notes: Cytotoxic backbone with vinCRIStine (Packer-type carboplatin/vincristine regimen). No per-drug dose is printed in the cited sources, so basis, dose, unit, and days are VERIFY (carboplatin is commonly AUC- or BSA-dosed; the basis itself is not established here). ISMP tall-man CARBOplatin (do not confuse with CISplatin). Carboplatin hypersensitivity risk rises with cumulative exposure in this population.

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer 12th ed.
provenance.locator: devita.txt line 241008 (vincristine plus carboplatin most common first-line regimen); no per-drug dose printed

drugs.notes: Cytotoxic backbone with carboplatin. No per-drug dose printed, so basis, dose, unit, and days are VERIFY. ISMP tall-man vinCRIStine; 2 mg per-dose cap carried as a StewardMD safety rule; vinCRIStine is IV only and fatal if given intrathecally. Monitor for peripheral neuropathy and constipation.

drugs.name: Dabrafenib (BRAF V600E-mutated tumors only)

provenance.locator: ped_cns.txt lines 1203, 1209 to 1211 (If BRAF V600E mutated: Dabrafenib/Trametinib); discussion of combined BRAF/MEK blockade with dabrafenib and trametinib lines 3030 to 3043; no pediatric dose printed

drugs.notes: Biomarker-gated: given ONLY for BRAF V600E-mutated tumors, in combination with the MEK inhibitor trametinib. No pediatric weight/BSA dose printed in the cited extract, so basis, dose, unit, and days are VERIFY. Monitor for pyrexia, cutaneous toxicity, and (with combination) LVEF/ocular effects.

drugs.name: Trametinib (MEK inhibitor; combined with dabrafenib for BRAF V600E)

provenance.locator: ped_cns.txt lines 1203, 1210 (Dabrafenib/Trametinib for BRAF V600E mutated); combined BRAF/MEK blockade discussion lines 3030 to 3043; no pediatric dose printed

drugs.notes: MEK inhibitor combined with dabrafenib for BRAF V600E-mutated tumors; MEK inhibition is also the rational target for BRAF-fusion (KIAA1549::BRAF) MAPK-activated tumors. No pediatric dose printed, so basis, dose, unit, and days are VERIFY. Monitor for rash, LVEF reduction, and ocular toxicity; resistance can emerge via MAPK reactivation (ped_cns.txt lines 3028 to 3032).

supportiveCare: carboplatin hypersensitivity surveillance across repeated cycles in this population
vinCRIStine: IV only, never intrathecal; monitor peripheral neuropathy and constipation

targeted therapy: BRAF/MEK-inhibitor toxicity monitoring (pyrexia, rash, LVEF, ocular); MAPK-pathway reactivation can drive resistance after initial BRAF-inhibition response (ped_cns.txt lines 3028 to 3032)
radiation-avoiding intent in young children: prefer chemotherapy first line to spare neurocognitive/endocrine late effects (devita.txt line 241008)

monitoring: serial brain (and spine if indicated) MRI for response and progression
CBC with platelets before each carboplatin/vinCRIStine cycle
peripheral neuropathy assessment before each vinCRIStine dose
BRAF/MEK-inhibitor toxicity monitoring (skin, pyrexia, LVEF, ophthalmologic) when targeted therapy is used
visual/endocrine assessment for optic-pathway and hypothalamic tumors

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Manage carboplatin hypersensitivity and cytopenia per institution; physician decides. Per-drug pediatric doses are VERIFY.

doseModificationRules.condition: BRAF/MEK-inhibitor grade >=3 toxicity (pyrexia, LVEF drop, ocular)
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and reduce targeted therapy per toxicity; physician decides. Doses are VERIFY.

core.locator: harrison.txt lines 102926 to 102938 (pilocytic astrocytoma WHO grade 1, most common childhood tumor; cerebellum/optic nerve/brainstem; frequent BRAF fusions or mutations; BRAF V600E targetable; curable if completely resected), 103006 to 103008 (observe versus resect); line 37573 (optic nerve glioma usually pilocytic astrocytoma). DeVita 12th ed. devita.txt line 241008 (vincristine plus carboplatin most common first-line regimen; chemotherapy preferred over radiotherapy in young children) and line 244896 (HIT-LGG carboplatin-vincristine)

guideline.locator: ped_cns.txt: BRAF V600E targeted therapy Dabrafenib/Trametinib (lines 1203, 1209 to 1211), molecular alterations of significance in pediatric gliomas including BRAF V600E mutation and BRAF fusion (lines 906 to 907), NTRK/other MAPK targets (lines 507 to 508, 915), combined BRAF/MEK blockade discussion (lines 3028 to 3043). NOTE: this extract's dedicated regimen tables cover pediatric diffuse high-grade gliomas and medulloblastoma; the pediatric low-grade glioma carboplatin/vincristine backbone is grounded from the DeVita/Harrison core layer.

provenanceNote: PEDIATRIC. StewardMD draft for pediatric low-grade glioma. Identity, histology, setting, and the BRAF gate are grounded: pilocytic astrocytoma (WHO grade 1) is the most common childhood tumor and frequently carries BRAF fusions or mutations, with BRAF V600E targetable (Harrison 22nd ed. harrison.txt lines 102926 to 102938); vinCRIStine plus carboplatin is the most common first-line regimen for progressive childhood low-grade glioma, with chemotherapy preferred over radiotherapy in young children (DeVita 12th ed. devita.txt line 241008, HIT-LGG line 244896); and BRAF V600E-mutated tumors are eligible for dabrafenib + trametinib (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Pediatric CNS Cancers v1.2026, ped_cns.txt lines 1203, 1209 to 1211). No per-drug pediatric dose is printed in the cited sources for the carboplatin/vinCRIStine backbone or the BRAF/MEK-inhibitor option, so all basis, dose, unit, and day fields are the literal VERIFY (listed in verifyFields) and were NOT invented; cycleLengthDays and cycles are VERIFY. Only the ISMP vinCRIStine 2 mg per-dose cap is carried. The pediatric CNS extract's regimen tables cover high-grade gliomas and medulloblastoma, so the low-grade-glioma cytotoxic backbone is grounded from the DeVita/Harrison core layer, transparently noted in evidence. NCCN per-disease template alignment, StewardMD clinical (R1) review, and any hospital-implementation overlay approval are pending. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
